message.content:
A CPU (Central Processing Unit) and a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) are both processors, but they’re designed for different kinds of workloads:

| Feature | CPU | GPU |
|---------|-----|-----|
| **Primary purpose** | General‑purpose computing – handles everything from OS tasks to application logic. | Parallel graphics rendering – originally for rasterizing images, now also for massively parallel compute tasks. |
| **Core count** | Few (2–32) high‑performance cores optimized for single‑thread speed. | Hundreds to thousands of simpler cores optimized for throughput. |
| **Clock speed** | High clock rates (3–5 GHz) to finish individual tasks quickly. | Lower clock rates (1–2 GHz) but many cores to process many data elements simultaneously. |
| **Instruction set** | Complex, with sophisticated branch prediction, out‑of‑order execution, large caches. | Simpler, highly SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data) – same instruction applied to many data points. |
| **Memory hierarchy** | Large L1/L2/L3 caches per core, deep memory hierarchy, low latency. | Smaller per‑core caches, larger shared memory, higher bandwidth but higher latency. |
| **Typical workloads** | Sequential tasks, branching logic, OS kernel, database queries, web servers. | Matrix/vector operations, image/video processing, machine‑learning inference/training, scientific simulations. |
| **Energy efficiency** | Optimized for low power per core but high performance per watt for single‑thread tasks. | Optimized for throughput per watt – many cores doing the same thing efficiently. |
| **Programming model** | Traditional imperative programming, multi‑threading with locks/threads. | Data‑parallel programming (CUDA, OpenCL, Vulkan compute, Metal, DirectCompute). |

In short, a CPU is a few very powerful cores that excel at handling diverse, sequential tasks with low latency, while a GPU is a large array of simpler cores that excel at performing the same operation on many data items in parallel, giving it huge raw throughput for tasks that can be parallelized.
